title: Analyzing Immune Cell Infiltration in 3D Pancreatic Heterotypic Spheroids
author: Thomas, Nadia, et al.

steps.title: Seed PDAC cells and CAFs
steps.instruction: On day 0, seed PDAC cells together with primary or immortalized CAFs in a 96‑well clear round‑bottom ultra‑low attachment plate at a ratio of 1:50 or 1:30 (cancer cells : CAFs, depending on the cancer cell line).

steps.title: Prepare spheroid dissociation buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the buffer extemporaneously by diluting 10× 0.5 % trypsin‑EDTA in Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free PBS to obtain a final trypsin concentration of 2×, then add collagenase IV to a final concentration of 40 µg mL⁻¹. Keep the buffer on ice until use.

steps.title: Prepare intracellular staining buffers
steps.instruction: Fixation/Permeabilization buffer: mix 1 part of the concentrate with 3 parts of Diluent to obtain a 1× working solution. Permeabilization buffer: mix 1 part of 10× Permeabilization Buffer with 9 parts distilled water to obtain a 1× working solution. Prepare fresh immediately before staining.

steps.title: Add PBMCs to spheroids
steps.instruction: On day 6, add peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to each well at a 1:10 ratio (CAFs + cancer cells : PBMCs) together with interleukin‑2 (IL‑2) to a final concentration of 10 ng mL⁻¹.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the cryovial containing frozen PBMCs from liquid nitrogen to a 37 °C water bath and thaw quickly.
Immediately transfer the thawed cells into a 15 mL centrifuge tube containing 10 mL of culture medium.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min, discard the DMSO‑containing supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of culture medium and count viable cells using a Malassez chamber (or equivalent) after trypan‑blue staining.
Prepare a suspension of 30 000 PBMCs in 50 µL of culture medium per well; add IL‑2 to reach 10 ng mL⁻¹ if not already present.
Using a multichannel pipette, dispense 50 µL of the PBMC suspension into each well containing the heterotypic spheroids.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 2 days without any centrifugation step.

steps.title: Wash spheroids and remove non‑infiltrated PBMCs
steps.instruction: On day 8, collect spheroids, wash three times with Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free PBS at room temperature to discard non‑infiltrated (OUT) PBMCs, and transfer spheroids to a 24‑well plate for dissociation.

substeps.instruction: Collect spheroids as described in step 1 (use the same method).
Allow spheroids to settle by gravity for 2–3 min, then aspirate the supernatant carefully (avoid disturbing the pellet).
Add 5 mL of 1× Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free PBS (20‑25 °C) to rinse; let spheroids settle again and aspirate. Repeat this wash three times.
Coat 300 µL pipette tips by aspirating 200 µL of Anti‑Adherence Rinsing Solution, then wash the tips with 200 µL of 1× Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free PBS.

Transfer all spheroids of the same experimental condition (maximum ~100 µL total volume) into a single well of a 24‑well plate; avoid large residual PBS volumes that could dilute the dissociation enzymes.
Count and record the number of spheroids per condition using a light or stereomicroscope.
Place the 24‑well plate in a cold room (4‑8 °C) or on ice for 20 min before enzymatic dissociation.

steps.title: Enzymatic dissociation of spheroids
steps.instruction: Dissociate spheroids on ice using the prepared spheroid dissociation buffer, then neutralize trypsin with FBS and collect a single‑cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL of cold spheroid dissociation buffer (2× trypsin + 40 µg mL⁻¹ collagenase IV) to each well.
Incubate on ice (4‑8 °C) for 20 min.
Vigorously pipette up and down with a multichannel pipette equipped with four 200 µL tips until the spheroids are completely dissociated; verify under a light microscope.
If dissociation is incomplete, incubate an additional 5–10 min on ice and repeat the pipetting step until a single‑cell suspension is achieved.
Add 300 µL of fetal bovine serum (FBS) to inactivate trypsin.
Transfer the suspension to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube and centrifuge at 300 × g, 21‑25 °C for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and keep the cell pellet on ice.

steps.title: Phenotypic flow cytometry staining
steps.instruction: Stain the dissociated cells for surface markers, fix/permeabilize, then stain intracellular markers according to the immunophenotyping panel (Table 3).

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 100 µL of Fc block diluted 1:100 in FACS buffer; incubate on ice for 30 min.
Prepare the extracellular antibody mix in FACS buffer using the volumes listed in Table 3 (per 0.5 × 10⁶ cells in 100 µL). Keep the mix on ice and protected from light.
Add 100 µL of the extracellular antibody mix to each sample (add 100 µL FACS buffer to the unstained negative control). Incubate on ice, 4 °C, in the dark for 30 min.
Wash twice: add 100 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 300 × g, 4 °C, 3 min; discard supernatant by flipping the plate and gently dry.
Add 100 µL of 1× Fixation/Permeabilization Buffer; mix gently and incubate in the dark for 20‑30 min.
Without washing, add 100 µL of 1× Permeabilization Buffer; centrifuge 300 × g, 4 °C, 3 min; discard supernatant.
Wash once with 150 µL of 1× Permeabilization Buffer (same centrifugation conditions).
Prepare the intracellular antibody mix in 1× Permeabilization Buffer using the volumes listed in Table 3; keep on ice and protected from light.
Add 100 µL of the intracellular antibody mix to each sample, mix gently, and incubate at room temperature (20‑25 °C) in the dark for 1 h.
Wash twice with 100 µL of 1× Permeabilization Buffer; centrifuge 300 × g, 4 °C, 3 min each time; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the final pellet in 150 µL of FACS buffer containing 1 % paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Optional pause point: store stained cells in FACS buffer‑1 % PFA at 4 °C, protected from light, for up to 7 days (preferably process sooner).
Add 10 µL of Precision Count Beads™ to each sample.
Acquire data on a Cytoflex LX flow cytometer (or equivalent).
Analyze using the gating strategy shown in Figure 5; quantify infiltrating immune cells using the formula described in steps 3j‑m (i.e., bead‑based absolute counting).

Note: Prior to staining, generate a compensation matrix for all fluorophores (using compensation beads or singly stained cells) and run Fluorescence Minus One (FMO) controls at least once per antibody panel.

steps.title: Functional flow cytometry staining
steps.instruction: Assess cytokine production and degranulation markers in infiltrating immune cells using the functional panel (Table 4).

substeps.instruction: For each condition, use 192 spheroids (two 96‑well plates) to obtain sufficient infiltrating cells.
Add BD GolgiStop™ Protein Transport Inhibitor (1:3000) and GolgiPlug™ Protein Transport Inhibitor (1:2000) directly to the wells containing spheroids.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 4 h (do not exceed 12 h total culture after inhibitor addition).
Harvest spheroids and dissociate them exactly as described in steps 5‑6 (wash, cold dissociation buffer, incubation, pipetting, FBS neutralization, centrifugation).

Stain the resulting single‑cell suspension following the same sequence as the phenotypic staining (steps 6‑14 of the phenotypic protocol), but use the antibody volumes listed in Table 4 (per 0.5 × 10⁶ cells in 100 µL FACS buffer).
Proceed with acquisition and analysis as described for phenotypic staining, focusing on intracellular IFN‑γ, Granzyme B, CD107a, and surface PD‑1 expression.

description: The tumor microenvironment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a complex structure implicated in the resistance to current treatments.1,2 Therefore, the development of new therapeutic approaches to circumvent resistance is a real challenge, particularly because only few in vitro models that mimic the complex interactions in the PDAC ecosystem are currently available. Yet, such models might allow the development of large-scale drug screening to identify new therapeutic strategies.3 In recent years, efforts have been made to generate 2D and 3D co-culture models of tumor cells with cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs), which show very interesting pro-tumor effects. These in vitro models are very relevant,3,4 but they lack an immune compartment to reproduce as closely as possible the tumor microenvironment and the complex crosstalk among the different cell populations.5 We present a detailed protocol to generate complex heterotypic 3D models of PDAC (Figure 1). These models reconstitute the complex interactions between cancer cells and stroma components (i.e., CAFs and immune cells). They are composed of PDAC cells (commercial cell lines or established from patient-derived xenografts), primary or immortalized CAFs, and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) isolated from healthy donors. We outline the flow cytometry steps used to determine the cell ratios, an information required to identify the optimal culture conditions, and the immunophenotyping strategy to measure immune infiltration and perform the functional characterization with quantitative accuracy.
